label: yes
controls_available: START ENGINE starts the active simulation.
LEFT, CENTER, and RIGHT are persistent steering buttons.
BRAKE, COAST, and THROTTLE are persistent pedal buttons.
FILE DELIVERY submits the current replay and NEW DELIVERY starts an administrative retry after failure.
autonomous_processes: After the engine starts, requestAnimationFrame/pump advances the simulation by 20 ms physics ticks without a new agent action.
The two generated horizontal traffic streams advance continuously; each driver recomputes conflict-based braking against the ego and other traffic, changing its speed and position.
The ego advances under the persistent steering and pedal settings, while each tick checks collision, road-edge, arrival, and timeout status.
grouped_control_modes: D: all outcome-affecting simplified panel_buttons control changes across every seed, action boundary, round, and retry: persistent steering (LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT) and pedal (BRAKE/COAST/THROTTLE).
START ENGINE, FILE DELIVERY, and NEW DELIVERY are administrative lifecycle controls rather than outcome-affecting members of D.

clause_i.reason: The same own-action history I_t can occur with different generated turns, traffic phases, speeds, and yield horizons. Near a junction gap, one visible traffic state makes a throttle/turn commit optimal while another makes brake/coast or different turn timing optimal. A policy q(I_t) cannot inspect that state, so no action-only q is optimal for every history in C_Delta(D).

clause_ii.reason: The configured five chronological frames over 400 ms visibly expose traffic displacement, direction, and red brake-light responses on the canvas. Tracking that bounded recent trajectory lets g predict whether a stream is closing or yielding and choose the delayed persistent panel setting; it uses the same traffic evolution as clauses (i) and (iii).

clause_iii.reason: Within an active crossing opportunity, take a=THROTTLE while steering is set for the selected departure. During a positive subinterval of the 400 ms horizon, traffic continues into or away from the conflict geometry and its braking state changes; success can remain possible with another control, while the same commit can become collision-prone or less effective. The strict loss is caused by moving traffic and vehicle state, not by a deadline or mere later completion.

common_visible_process: Responsive cross traffic moves through the junction while the ego vehicle is committed to a turn. Its recent canvas trajectory and brake-light state reveal whether a gap is closing or being yielded; waiting can turn an initially useful throttle/turn action into a worse action even though braking, coasting, or re-steering can still recover the delivery.

pre_run.reason: The rendered model starts with control [0,0], and setControl returns while the simulation is not started, so simplified panel settings cannot be prepared before START ENGINE. With no outcome-affecting action after start, pedal=0 keeps the ego speed at zero under the clamped drag update and its position stays at (480,470); generated goals are at y=190 for a left turn or y=260 for a right turn. No generated instance can arrive under the pre-run protocol, so the 50% override is not met.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 3 has two lanes, three cars per lane, 34-48 speed, 1.3-2.1 yield horizons, both turn directions, and road_half 90.
The exact simplified surface uses persistent steering and pedal proxy buttons; the configured observation window is 400 ms with five frames.
Seeded generation randomizes the turn, traffic phases, speeds, yield horizons, deceleration, and lane traffic while preserving the selected difficulty parameters.
The generated world starts the ego at (480,470) with zero speed, has 20 ms physics and a 6000-tick cap, and places the selected turn goal on the left or right departure road.
Each active tick updates conflict-based traffic braking, ego kinematics, traffic position, and terminal status; pump advances ticks from elapsed 20 ms task time, and control changes persist.
Cars are visibly drawn with braking-dependent red rear lights, and the canvas draws the moving traffic, ego, road, and selected departure goal.
The simplified render creates the six persistent panel buttons, initializes control [0,0], ignores control changes before start, and records panel input as panel_buttons.
The authoritative replay uses dt=.02, moves both ego and traffic, changes braking and speed, and checks physical intersection, road edge, goal arrival, and timeout.
The grader binds the simplified transcript to panel_buttons and accepts success only when the replayed physical state is arrived.
The privileged planner scores candidate controls by simulating 100-tick continuations including braking drivers, showing that traffic state affects control choice.
For simplified mode the solver changes panel inputs and reevaluates every 100 ms after starting, rather than relying on one pre-run setting.
Verification loads the exported result and the independent Courtesy Junction replay grader; it does not replace the physical outcome contract.
